services.name: Drain Cleaning
services.h1: Drain Cleaning in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Drain Cleaning, Round Rock, TX | Round Rock Plumbing Company
services.meta: Round Rock Plumbing Company clears slow, gurgling, and smelly drains in Round Rock, TX, with checks for clogs in sinks, tubs, showers, and floor drains.
services.blurb: Clearing slow, gurgling, and backed-up drains across Round Rock.

paragraphs: A sink that gurgles, a shower that holds water, or a drain with a sewage smell points to a blockage or venting issue. Grease, soap residue, hair, and mineral scale can narrow the pipe until water cannot move normally.

We clear drains in Round Rock, Brushy Creek, Windemere, and Wells Branch. A slow drain in one fixture can sometimes wait, but water backing into a tub, shower, or floor drain should not wait because wastewater can overflow into the room.

sections.heading: Gurgling sink and tub backup
paragraphs: Customers often report a kitchen sink that drains slowly, a shower pan filling around their feet, or a bathroom sink that makes a gurgling sound. Other common signs include a floor drain with standing water, a foul smell from a fixture, and water rising in one drain while another fixture runs.

A clog in a trap, a blocked branch line, and a restricted vent can produce similar sounds and backups. The repair work and materials differ, so we inspect the fixture and pipe route before identifying what needs clearing.

sections.heading: Fixture inspection and cable work
paragraphs: We start at the affected sink, tub, shower, or floor drain. We check the trap, stopper, strainer, drain opening, cleanout, and visible pipe joints. We run water to see how quickly the fixture drains and note whether another drain reacts.

A basic trap check may take about 15 minutes. Cable cleaning for an accessible branch line often takes 30 to 90 minutes, depending on the blockage and pipe route. We can usually clear an accessible clog during the visit, and may replace a worn trap washer or damaged cleanout plug if needed. A blockage beyond the available cleanout, or one requiring a camera inspection, may need a separate visit with the right equipment.

sections.heading: Cleanout access and pipe route
paragraphs: The cleanout location affects the work. A cleanout in a garage, utility room, or exterior wall gives us a more direct path than a line reached only through a sink trap or tight cabinet.

Pipe material also matters. Older cast-iron pipe can collect scale inside the wall of the line, while plastic pipe may have a different fitting layout or access point. A seized cleanout plug, a buried access point, or a blockage deep in a long branch line adds labor and may require additional equipment.

sections.heading: Fixture and cleanout location
paragraphs: Tell us which room and fixture is draining slowly or backing up. Let us know whether the kitchen sink, shower, tub, bathroom sink, or floor drain is affected.
Check whether water is standing in the basin, pan, or floor drain now. Note if running the dishwasher, washing machine, or another faucet makes the problem appear in a different fixture.

If you know where the cleanout is, mention whether it is outside, in a garage, under a cabinet, or behind an access panel. A photo of the drain opening, stopper, or visible pipe can also help us prepare.
Call Round Rock Plumbing Company at (512) 882-1291 before a slow drain turns into wastewater backing up across the floor.

services.name: Water Heater Repair
services.h1: Water Heater Repair in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Water Heater | Round Rock Plumbing Company, Round Rock, TX
services.meta: Round Rock Plumbing Company repairs tank and tankless water heaters in Round Rock, TX, including leaks, cold water, burner faults, elements, and valves.
services.blurb: Tank and tankless water heater repairs for leaks, cold water, and failed controls.

paragraphs: A cold shower and a wet water-heater closet can both get called a broken water heater. Cold water at every hot tap points toward a heating, fuel, or control fault. A pan filling beneath the tank points toward a leak. We handle both problems in Round Rock, Brushy Creek, Windemere, and Wells Branch.

Rust-colored water, a burner that will not stay lit, or a breaker that trips can also stop hot water without a tank leak. We trace the fault from the shutoff and supply lines to the controls, heating elements, burner, or tank.

A leaking tank or relief valve should not wait because water can spread into drywall, flooring, and framing. A heater that only makes lukewarm water can sometimes wait briefly, but it still needs diagnosis before a failed element, burner, or valve leaves the home without hot water.

sections.heading: No hot water or banging
paragraphs: People call us for no hot water, water that turns cold halfway through a shower, banging or popping from the tank, and water pooling around the base. A rotten-egg smell at the hot tap, a pilot light that goes out, or a breaker that trips are different clues.

These symptoms can overlap, but sediment, a failed element, a gas control fault, a relief valve, and a tank seam are not the same repair. The needed parts and repair cost can differ widely, even when the problem sounds similar over the phone.

sections.heading: Tank inspection and test
paragraphs: We begin a tank inspection by reading the model plate and checking the cold supply, hot outlet, shutoff, drain valve, relief valve, and visible pipe joints. We read incoming water pressure at a gauge and compare outlet temperature with the thermostat setting, which is commonly around 120°F. On a tankless unit, we also check the display code, inlet screen, vent connection, and condensate line where fitted.

A diagnostic check generally takes 20 to 40 minutes. We can often replace an accessible thermostat, heating element, thermocouple, pilot assembly, or relief valve during the same visit if the matching part is available. An element replacement after draining the tank can take 45 to 90 minutes. Tank replacement, corroded pipe changes, or controls that must be ordered are scheduled for another visit.

sections.heading: Anode rods, shutoffs, access
paragraphs: The age and condition of the anode rod, gas control, elements, or tank seam affect the scope of a repair. An accessible thermostat behind a lower panel is a different job from a corroded fitting on an older tank. A unit in a tight attic, raised platform, closet, or finished utility room also takes more setup than a heater with clear floor access.

A seized shutoff can require pipe work before we can isolate the heater safely. A discontinued control, uncommon element, or tankless component may need to be ordered. If a replacement requires permit or inspection sign-off, the job also involves coordination beyond the heater itself.

sections.heading: Model plate and access
paragraphs: We can use the model number, serial number, and fuel type to identify the correct water-heater parts. On many units, the rating plate is printed on the tank jacket, near the gas control, or beside the electrical panel.

Tell us which room holds the heater and whether it is in a garage, closet, attic, or utility room. Let us know if water is running from the tank, relief valve, or nearby pipe, and whether the shutoff will turn.
Call Round Rock Plumbing Company at (512) 882-1291 with the model plate details; a leaking tank can continue soaking flooring, drywall, and framing while it waits.

services.name: Pipe Leak Repair
services.h1: Pipe Leak Repair in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Leak Repair | Round Rock Plumbing Company | Round Rock, TX
services.meta: Round Rock Plumbing Company handles pipe leak repair in Round Rock, TX, tracing wet walls, failed fittings, and hidden water lines before damage spreads.
services.blurb: We trace and repair leaking pipes before water damages walls, cabinets, and floors.

paragraphs: A slow drip under a sink can leave a cabinet floor swollen within a week. A small wet spot on drywall can spread along a stud bay over a month, loosening paint, staining ceilings, and wetting insulation.

Water can also escape behind a shower wall or beneath a slab without a visible puddle. Pipe leaks should not wait because moisture keeps moving through framing, drywall, flooring, and cabinets until the source is isolated.

sections.heading: Water stains and hissing
paragraphs: Customers often call about a brown ceiling ring, a damp cabinet base, or a hissing sound behind a wall. Other signs include paint bubbling near a baseboard, a warm patch on a floor, or a water meter that moves after every fixture is off.

A drip at a supply connection, a split pipe joint, and a leak inside a wall can look similar from the room side. We inspect the pipe and fitting because each fault needs a different repair and can involve different parts and access.

sections.heading: Leak inspection and pressure test
paragraphs: We start a leak inspection by checking the water meter, visible supply lines, shutoff valves, fixture connections, cabinets, and nearby drywall. We isolate sections of piping where possible and use a pressure gauge to see whether the system loses pressure with faucets closed.

A basic exposed-leak check can take about 15 to 30 minutes. Finding a concealed leak can take longer because we trace moisture through wall cavities, ceiling framing, or flooring before opening a surface.

We can usually replace an exposed supply line, valve, compression fitting, or accessible section of pipe on the same visit. A pipe run behind tile, inside a wall, below a slab, or requiring ordered material is scheduled for return work after the leak location and access route are confirmed.

sections.heading: Pipe access and shutoff valves
paragraphs: The pipe material, fitting age, and location of the leak affect the scope of repair. A corroded copper joint, brittle plastic fitting, or damaged supply line may need a different connection method and replacement part.
Easy access under a sink or in a utility room keeps the work focused on the failed section. A leak behind tile, drywall, cabinets, or insulation requires more time to reach and test.

A seized shutoff valve can add work because water must be controlled before a fitting is removed. Parts that need ordering, as well as any required inspection or sign-off, also change the work involved.

sections.heading: Fixture room and pipe material
paragraphs: Tell us which room has the wet wall, stain, hissing sound, or damp cabinet. Let us know which fixture is closest, such as a sink, shower, washing machine, or refrigerator line.
If you can see the pipe, note whether it is copper, plastic, or braided supply hose. Check whether water is actively running and whether the shutoff valve or access panel is reachable.

A photo of the fitting and the surrounding cabinet or wall can help us prepare for the visit. Call Round Rock Plumbing Company at (512) 882-1291 before a continuing leak turns a small wet area into damaged drywall, flooring, or framing.

services.name: Toilet Repair
services.h1: Toilet Repair in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Toilet Repair | Round Rock Plumbing Company | Round Rock, TX
services.meta: At Round Rock Plumbing Company, we handle toilet repair in Round Rock, TX, including running tanks, weak flushes, base leaks, and fill valves.
services.blurb: We repair running, leaking, and poorly flushing toilets in Round Rock.

paragraphs: A plunger is the sensible first step for a bowl that is slow to clear or has stopped flushing. It can move a soft blockage through the trap, and it costs nothing to try. The plunger stops helping if the bowl fills again, the handle does nothing, or water appears at the base.

We check the tank, bowl, supply line, and floor around the fixture to find the failed part. A toilet with ongoing water flow, a leak, or a failed flush should not wait, because it can waste water, soak flooring, or leave a bathroom without a working fixture.

sections.heading: Toilet keeps running
paragraphs: We hear about toilets that keep running after the flush, bowls that will not refill, handles that move without flushing, and water around the toilet base. A tank that hisses may have a worn fill valve, while a quiet tank that refills every few minutes may have a leaking flapper or flush-valve seal.

A weak flush can come from a low tank water level, a disconnected lift chain, or mineral buildup in the rim holes. Water on the floor may come from a supply connector, tank bolt, wax ring, or a cracked bowl. These faults can look alike from outside the fixture, but the parts and labor involved are not the same.

sections.heading: Fixture inspection and test
paragraphs: We start with a fixture inspection and test. We flush the toilet several times, check the tank water level, inspect the flapper and fill valve, and look for moisture at the supply connection, tank bolts, and base. We also check the shutoff valve and measure supply pressure, since household plumbing commonly runs between 40 and 80 psi.

A tank check often takes 15 to 30 minutes. We measure the flush-valve opening, which is commonly 2 or 3 inches, before fitting a flapper or seal. Standard flappers, fill valves, trip levers, supply connectors, and tank seals can often be replaced during the same visit. We schedule a further visit if a brand-specific part must be ordered or the toilet must be removed for a base leak.

sections.heading: Shutoff valves and tank parts
paragraphs: The age and design of the tank parts affect the work. A common flapper or fill valve is usually more straightforward than a discontinued flush valve, a concealed actuator, or a part made only for one toilet model. A tank lid or bowl that has cracked can also change the scope of the repair.

Access at the shutoff valve matters too. A seized angle stop may need replacement before we can safely work on the supply line. A leak at the base can require lifting the toilet to inspect the wax ring and floor flange, especially if the fixture rocks or the flooring has softened.

sections.heading: Tank model and bathroom access
paragraphs: Have the toilet model number available if you can find it. It is often stamped inside the tank or printed beneath the tank lid. Tell us which bathroom has the problem and whether the toilet is running, leaking, or failing to flush now.

Let us know the approximate age of the fixture and whether the shutoff valve is easy to reach behind the bowl. Clear a path to the bathroom if storage, rugs, or furniture block the fixture. Call us at (512) 882-1291 before a running tank keeps cycling water or a base leak has more time to soak the floor.

services.name: Sewer Line Repair
services.h1: Sewer Line Repair in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Sewer Repair | Round Rock Plumbing Company | Round Rock, TX
services.meta: Round Rock Plumbing Company handles sewer line repair in Round Rock, TX, using camera inspection to locate roots, breaks, and sewer backups.
services.blurb: Camera-led sewer line repair for backups, roots, breaks, and damaged pipe.

paragraphs: Most calls start with “the toilet flushes but the tub fills,” “there is a sewer smell in the yard,” or “water is coming up through the shower drain.” Those descriptions point beyond one fixture. We trace the building sewer, the pipe carrying wastewater from the house to the sewer main or septic connection.

Other callers notice a washing machine drain makes the toilet gurgle, or that several sinks drain slowly at once. A blocked, cracked, shifted, or root-filled sewer line can cause those symptoms. The camera and locator show where the trouble sits.
Sewage backing into a tub, shower, floor drain, or yard should not wait. Wastewater can keep moving through the pipe and spread into rooms or soil, making the affected section harder to repair.

sections.heading: Sewage in tubs and yards
paragraphs: Water rising in a shower after a toilet flush is a common report. So is a toilet that bubbles when the washing machine drains, a sewer odor near the cleanout, or a wet patch above the buried line. Each symptom gives us a different starting point for the inspection.

A slow sink alone may be a fixture drain issue, but several slow fixtures often point farther down the sewer pipe. A yard smell may come from a cracked joint, a loose cleanout cap, or sewage escaping from a damaged section. Gurgling can also come from a partial blockage that has not fully stopped flow.

These faults can sound alike over the phone, but they do not involve the same pipe section, equipment, or repair work. A camera inspection separates a root blockage from a broken pipe, a belly, or a failing connection before repair decisions are made.

sections.heading: Camera inspection and locating
paragraphs: We start at the cleanout where access allows. A camera head travels through the sewer pipe, and its footage shows roots, cracks, offsets, standing water, or collapsed sections. An accessible camera inspection often takes 20 to 40 minutes, depending on the pipe route and blockage.

We can use a locator above ground to mark the camera head and estimate the line route and depth. We check the cleanout, pipe material, visible joints, and the connection path toward the street or septic area. Camera work, locating, and accessible cleanout checks are usually handled during the visit; excavation, pipe replacement under a slab, permits, or required sign-off may need separate scheduling.

sections.heading: Pipe depth, material, access
paragraphs: Pipe material changes the repair approach. Clay tile can separate at joints, cast iron can corrode from the inside, and older Orangeburg pipe can deform or flatten. PVC usually has different connection and replacement requirements than those older materials.

Depth and access also affect the work. A line beneath open soil is different from a section under a driveway, foundation slab, tree roots, fencing, or landscaping. A seized cleanout, a difficult camera entry point, an ordered fitting, or municipal sign-off can add equipment, restoration, or return work to the repair.

sections.heading: Cleanout location and fixtures
paragraphs: Before calling, check which fixtures are affected: toilet, shower, tub, washing machine standpipe, or floor drain. Tell us whether sewage or water is rising now, and whether the problem started after laundry, a flush, or heavy water use.

If you can find the cleanout, note whether it is in the yard, garage, basement, or near an exterior wall. A cleanout is often a capped pipe near ground level, but its location varies by property. Let us know about gates, locked side yards, vehicles, concrete, or landscaping above the suspected pipe route.

Older home records or a prior camera report can help identify clay, cast iron, PVC, or Orangeburg pipe. Call Round Rock Plumbing Company at (512) 882-1291 before sewage reaches more fixtures, floors, or yard soil.

services.name: Garbage Disposal Repair
services.h1: Garbage Disposal Repair in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Disposal Repair | Round Rock Plumbing Company Round Rock, TX
services.meta: Round Rock Plumbing Company repairs humming, leaking, jammed garbage disposals in Round Rock, TX, Brushy Creek, Windemere, and Wells Branch.
services.blurb: We repair jammed, humming, leaking, and nonworking garbage disposals.

paragraphs: In Round Rock and Brushy Creek homes, garbage disposal trouble often starts with an original kitchen unit that has handled years of food scraps. The motor, mounting ring, splash guard, and drain connection all wear differently. A disposal can also fail after a utensil, fruit pit, or glass fragment drops through the sink opening.

We check the unit beneath the kitchen sink, the electrical connection, and the discharge pipe before recommending a repair or replacement. A humming unit can sometimes wait if the sink stays unused, but water under the cabinet or a sink that will not drain should not wait because the seal, drain fitting, or cabinet base can be damaged.

sections.heading: Humming disposal and sink water
paragraphs: We hear several versions of the same call: the disposal hums but will not spin, the reset button keeps popping, or nothing happens at the switch. Metal grinding inside the chamber usually points to a trapped object or worn grinding components. A sour smell can come from food caught below the splash guard, while water beneath the sink can come from the mounting ring, dishwasher connection, or discharge pipe.

Water rising in one side of a double-bowl sink can also appear to be a disposal failure. These symptoms can look alike from above the countertop, but the motor, seal, switch, and drain connection are separate faults with different repair work and parts.

sections.heading: Disposal inspection and test
paragraphs: We start the disposal inspection by isolating power and checking the switch, reset button, cord, and wiring connections. We test the electrical supply, inspect the motor housing, and look for leaks at the sink flange and discharge elbow. Initial testing and a cabinet inspection often take 20 to 40 minutes, depending on access and the condition of the fittings.

We can usually clear a jam, remove a lodged object, reset the unit, or tighten a loose mounting assembly during the same visit. A failed motor, cracked housing, or damaged mounting system may require a replacement unit or a part matched to the existing sink opening and drain connection.

sections.heading: Mounting ring, shutoff, and access
paragraphs: The age of the disposal affects the repair path because older motor housings, mounting rings, and wiring can be worn at the same time. A simple reset or jam removal involves less work than a unit with a failed motor or a leak at the sink flange. The make and model also matter if a splash guard, mounting component, or replacement unit must be matched.

Cabinet access changes the work involved. Packed cleaning supplies, fixed shelving, a tight double-bowl sink, or a seized dishwasher shutoff can add disassembly and testing. If a specific part must be ordered, or cabinet wiring needs code-required sign-off, we explain that before the next stage of work.

sections.heading: Model plate and sink cabinet
paragraphs: Before calling, check the model number on the disposal label, usually found on the side or underside of the motor housing. Tell us which kitchen sink has the problem and whether the unit hums, leaks, or stays completely silent. Note whether water is standing in the sink and whether the dishwasher is connected to the disposal. If possible, clear space beneath the sink so we can reach the outlet, reset button, mounting ring, and drain pipe. Call Round Rock Plumbing Company at (512) 882-1291 before a leak at the disposal damages the cabinet floor or spreads into the sink base.
